description:
Redwood Inference is taking its existing rollout primitives (model versioning, fallback routing, observability) and shipping a General Availability (GA) “Hosted canary rollout workflow” for percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes. The goal is to let customers safely introduce a new model version/config by gradually shifting traffic (e.g., 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%) with clear UI visibility, policy guardrails, and fast rollback. This project sits in Redwood Console (workflow/UI), Platform Control Plane (policy evaluation + configuration), Smart Routing/Data Plane (traffic splitting enforcement), and Telemetry/SRE (stop conditions, metrics, reliability).

Goals / outcomes:
- GA-ready Console workflow to create, run, pause, and rollback canary rollouts on Hosted routes.
- Policy controls for safe rollouts: max step size, minimum soak time, approval gates, and automatic stop/rollback based on SLO metrics (error rate, latency, timeouts) and optionally quality metrics.
- Auditable change history (who changed what, when), including audit log events and customer-visible rollout timeline.
- Clear metrics and comparisons between baseline and canary cohorts (per route/model version/region).
- Documentation updates (Console + API) and internal runbooks for on-call and support.

Non-goals (for GA scope):
- Full multi-armed bandits or dynamic traffic optimization.
- Deep quality-eval automation as a hard gate (supported as optional/manual inputs; automated quality gates can follow).
- Dedicated/Private rollout GA parity (ensure schema compatibility and minimize future migration pain, but Hosted is the GA target).

Key stakeholders:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (rollout policy + telemetry requirements)
- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & Tooling), Chloe Martin (Console Backend), Ethan Park (Platform Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)
- SRE/Infra: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (reliability, paging, runbooks)
- Security: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei (audit logs, policy enforcement visibility)
- Design/DX: Tessa Morgan / Kenji Nakamura (workflow UX), Elliot Price / Wei Chen (docs)

Phases / timeline (typical):
1) Discovery & requirements (2–3 weeks): define GA requirements, guardrails, auditability, and metrics.
2) Design & architecture (2–4 weeks): Console flow, policy schema, enforcement points, data model.
3) Implementation (4–8+ weeks): backend APIs, UI, routing enforcement, telemetry, tests.
4) Beta / design partners (2–6 weeks): limited rollout, iterate on guardrails, observability, and UX.
5) GA readiness (2–3 weeks): documentation, support enablement, runbooks, release notes, final go/no-go.

Deliverables:
- PRD + design spec + ADRs for rollout semantics and policy evaluation.
- Console UI and backend endpoints for rollout creation/execution.
- Routing enforcement for percentage splits per Hosted route with deterministic cohorting.
- Telemetry: metrics + dashboards + alerting and auto-stop/rollback wiring.
- Audit logs and access controls for who can start/approve rollouts.
- Docs and internal runbooks; launch checklist; post-beta retro.
